content.text: Why both tools have a modifier UI

inlineContent.text: Mocking Star and Merlin have separate mock servers and workspaces. A modifier created in
Mocking Star is not automatically available to Merlin’s test runner. Sharing the JavaScript
contract lets us reuse the transformation logic, but files, domains, and sample mock references
still belong to their respective workspaces.
Without Merlin Studio’s modifier editor, we could author in Mocking Star, copy the
file into Merlin, adapt its metadata/sample reference, and then run the flow. For repeated
authoring, that introduces manual synchronization and makes it easier to preview one version
while testing another. Studio allows authoring and previewing in the test’s own workspace,
so the saved file is the definition the CLI loads for that test.
This removes the need to move a file for every edit. It does not create an automatic
synchronization service between the two tools. A deliberate transfer is still possible.

To mock another route, keep/import that route’s recorded mock and select its domain/scenario
through the flow or a per-path fixture. Its own normal resolution still applies. The JFY
widget’s absolute full-service products URL creates a separate request and can need login;
Live on search widgets does not force that products route to Live.
The CLI validates the effective setup, including base includes and project defaults, before
device setup. Each attempt validates again and installs
for its device/domain
before cold launch. Deferred cleanup removes that set on completion, launch failure, retry or
cancellation. An empty list skips activation; the prior attempt’s cleanup prevents leakage.
The server’s activation state is process-local.
The inspected Android interceptor also checks the request host and seeded routing intent.
Flow defaults or a per-path scenario must resolve a routing selection; otherwise that
request proceeds directly to the backend. Only its allowed API hosts and stage-host suffix
are eligible. An absolute JFY URL is a separate route, but an arbitrary absolute URL is not
automatically routed through Merlin. Check the installed APK’s host rules, original path,
and seeded domain/scenario when a request never reaches the mock server.
Current Scylla implementation, checked on 8 November 2026:
activations are keyed by the
executor’s device serial. The CLI creates a dedicated host ingress for each device and reverses
the APK’s fixed local mock port to that ingress. The ingress supplies the correct serial,
overriding missing or stale
. The Android interceptor does not need to supply
that header for CLI-managed runs. Routing defaults and per-path scenarios are pre-staged in
preferences before launch, so eligible bootstrap requests use the correct activation set.
Relaunch and process restoration retain the mapping; server shutdown closes listeners and
device cleanup removes the reverse tunnel. Named activation buckets do not inherit the default.
This supersedes the presentation’s earlier default-bucket workaround and the previously
documented missing-header compatibility gap. Fake-bridge startup tests, real HTTP ingress
isolation tests and race checks cover the current implementation. They do not replace an
end-to-end Android/CI smoke test or real parallel-device verification. Use released CLI/APK
versions containing the compatible routing bootstrap and ingress changes; this guide does not
establish their release availability. The current iOS runner rejects
before
launch; Studio preview and Go engine support are separate.
